title: Retail Installment Contracts and Collateral Protection Insurance: Shortening of Payoff Statement Days
content:
On Retail Installment Contracts, a payoff statement is shortened according to the vehicle's insurance tracking record under Collateral Protection Insurance — the record's status and the lapse notices mailed on it.

**Rule.**

- When the contract's insurance tracking record is **force-placed** or in **lapse-notice** status, **5** days are taken from the statement days.
- When it is in neither status but a first or second lapse notice was mailed on it in the rolling 12 months ending on the quote date, **2** days are taken.
- Otherwise none are taken.

| Tracking record status on the quote date | First or second lapse notice in the rolling 12 months | Days taken |
|---|---|---|
| force-placed | any | 5 |
| lapse notice | any | 5 |
| compliant or any other status | one or more | 2 |
| compliant or any other status | none | 0 |

The rolling 12 months run from records dated later than the same calendar day 12 months before the quote date (the last day of that month when that day does not exist) through the quote date; only notices of the first-lapse and second-lapse kinds are counted.

**Hypothetical case.** A record back in compliant status, with a second lapse notice mailed seven months before the quote date: 2 days are taken. A record currently force-placed: 5 days, whatever the notices.
